stages.label: Kök Türük
stages.title: The name the Göktürks gave themselves
stages.text: Written in Old Turkic runes in the Orkhon inscriptions of the 8th century, among the oldest surviving texts in a Turkic language. It reads right to left.

stages.label: Kök: blue, sky
stages.title: Where our name comes from
stages.text: In Old Turkic, kök means both blue and the sky. The word is still used across the Turkic languages today.

stages.label: Shangyrak
stages.title: The crown of the yurt
stages.text: The wooden ring at the top of the yurt that holds its frame together. It appears on the flag of Kyrgyzstan and the emblem of Kazakhstan.

About.title: About the foundation
About.lede: Turkic Blue Foundation is a non-profit organisation run by an international community of volunteers, researchers and supporters.
intro: We document and share the culture, history and languages of the Turkic peoples, from the Balkans to Siberia, and we work to make this knowledge free and accurate.
We also respond to misinformation and stand up for the reputation and rights of Turkic communities.
Our work is open. Content is published under free licences, and decisions about funding will be made publicly by the foundation's members.
About.peopleText: The foundation is run by volunteers from several countries. [Board members and advisors to be announced.]
About.contactText: For questions, partnerships and press enquiries, write to [contact email].

Name.title: Why “Blue”
Name.lede: The Old Turkic word kök means both blue and the sky. The Göktürks, whose khaganate stretched across Central Asia between the 6th and 8th centuries, called themselves Kök Türük.
Name.text: The same word is used across the Turkic languages today, in Latin, Cyrillic and Arabic scripts. Our name follows it.
Name.caption: The word for blue or sky in Turkic languages

Projects.title: Projects by Turkic Blue Foundation
Projects.lede: Turkipedia is live. Turquoise News, the research network and the DAO are in development.

turkipedia.name: Turkipedia
turkipedia.summary: A free encyclopedia of the Turkic world, written and reviewed by volunteers.
body: Turkipedia covers the history, peoples, states, languages, literature, art and traditions of the Turkic world. Each article can exist in seven languages: Turkish, Azerbaijani, Kazakh, Uzbek, Uyghur, English and French.

Every edit is reviewed before it is published, every revision is kept, and every author is credited. The first articles were imported from Turkish Wikipedia, with attribution, and the community improves them from there.
points: 14,238 articles, with more languages being added
Review of every edit before publication
Full revision history and author credits
turkipedia.takePart: Anyone can write, translate or review articles. Create an account on Turkipedia to start.

turquoise-news.name: Turquoise News
turquoise-news.summary: An independent news service about the Turkic world.
body: Turquoise News will report on society, culture, science and current affairs across the Turkic world. It will be written by people who live there and published in Turkic languages, English and French.
It will also publish corrections, with sources, when coverage elsewhere gets facts about Turkic peoples wrong.
points: Reporting from Turkic regions by local contributors
Publication in Turkic languages, English and French
turquoise-news.takePart: We are looking for journalists, editors and translators. Contact us to contribute before the launch.

research-network.name: TurkicBlue Research Network
research-network.summary: A network for researchers in Turkic studies.
body: The TurkicBlue Research Network connects researchers in linguistics, history, archaeology, literature and the social sciences who work on the Turkic world.
It will provide shared bibliographies, archives and datasets, open-access publication with peer review, and workshops that bring researchers from different countries together.
points: Shared bibliographies, archives and open datasets
Workshops and joint projects across countries

facts.label: Fields
facts.value: Linguistics, history, archaeology, literature, social sciences

research-network.takePart: Researchers and institutions can register their interest now.

dao.name: TurkicBlue DAO
dao.summary: The foundation's governance system on Ethereum.
body: The TurkicBlue DAO will let members of the foundation propose and vote on how its funds are spent and which projects it supports.
Proposals, votes and payments will be recorded on the Ethereum blockchain, so anyone can check them.
points: Open discussion in all working languages
dao.takePart: Subscribe to updates to hear when membership opens.

Governance.title: Governance
Governance.lede: The foundation will be governed by its members through a DAO, a decentralised autonomous organisation, on the Ethereum blockchain.
Governance.text: Members will decide how funds are spent and which projects the foundation supports. Every proposal, vote and payment will be public. The model follows the kurultay, the assembly in which Turkic peoples historically made major decisions together.

steps.title: Proposal
steps.text: A member submits a proposal: a project, a grant or a rule change.

steps.title: Discussion
steps.text: Members discuss it openly, in any of the working languages.

steps.title: Vote
steps.text: Members vote on chain. The result is binding and public.

steps.title: Implementation
steps.text: The foundation carries it out and reports on the outcome.

faq.a: A decentralised autonomous organisation is a set of rules that runs on a blockchain. Members submit proposals and vote, and the results are recorded publicly and carried out according to those rules.
Ethereum is widely used for this kind of governance and has established tools for proposals, voting and shared funds.
Membership will be open to the community. [Membership model and requirements to be decided.]
